introduction: On this Sunday, the prophet Jeremiah is thrown into a muddy well for speaking God's word, and a foreigner rescues him. In the Gospel, Jesus says he has come to bring fire on the earth, and that his word will cause division even within families. The Letter to the Hebrews urges us to run the race with perseverance, keeping our eyes fixed on Jesus. Let us follow Christ faithfully, whatever it costs.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord hears our cry and lifts us from the pit. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that the fire of God's love may burn in her and spread to the whole world. Let us pray to the Lord.
For prophets of our time, who speak the truth at great cost: that God may protect them and send people to help them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For families divided by faith or by conflict: that they may find reconciliation in Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are sinking in despair, like Jeremiah in the mud: that God may lift them up and set their feet on rock. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may run the race with perseverance, keeping our eyes fixed on Jesus. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, your Son came to set the earth on fire with your love. Strengthen us to follow him faithfully, and to run the race with our eyes fixed on him. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Looking to Jesus
reflection.body:
Jeremiah tells the people of Jerusalem a hard truth during a siege, and the officials want him dead. With the king's permission, they lower him into a cistern: "In the dungeon there was no water, but mire; and Jeremiah sank in the mire." Then an unexpected rescuer appears: Ebedmelech, an Ethiopian servant in the king's household, who speaks up for the prophet and pulls him out. The psalm could be Jeremiah's own song: "He brought me up also out of a horrible pit, out of the miry clay. He set my feet on a rock."

In the Gospel, Jesus speaks with intensity: "I came to throw fire on the earth. I wish it were already kindled." The fire is the love of God and the Holy Spirit, but it also purifies and divides. He speaks of the baptism he must undergo, his Passion, "and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!"

Then he says something surprising: "Do you think that I have come to give peace on the earth? I tell you, no, but rather division." Jesus is the Prince of Peace, but following him can create conflict, even in families, when some choose him and others reject him. Many Christians know this pain.

The Letter to the Hebrews encourages us to keep going. We are "surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses," the saints who have gone before us. So we must "run with perseverance the race that is set before us, looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross." When we grow tired, we look at him.

This week, if your faith causes tension with someone you love, pray for them with patience. And when you feel you are sinking, cry out to the Lord, who lifts us from the mud.
